page.overview:
What is Esgalduin?

Esgalduin was the main river of Doriath. It flowed from the hills of Dorthonion through Doriath past the caves of Menegroth under the Stone Bridge leading to the gates of the city; finally meeting up with the River Sirion in the west.

The Esgalduin had two unnamed upper branches of its own in Ered Gorgoroth. One ran along the border between Dor Dínen and Nan Dungortheb, and the other ran west for about 20 miles from the mountains into Nan Dungortheb and further south-east until merging with the first.

In a manuscript dating from the late 1950's and early 1960's, Tolkien wrote that Esgalduin is Sindarin for "the river under shade".

In earlier etymologies, Esgalduin was said to be Ilkorin for "River under Veil (of [?leaves])", consisting of the elements esgal ("screen, hiding, roof of leaves") + duin ("water, river").
